name: Add a plugin-provided Knowledge skill
query: My plugin currently stores a transcription prompt in an option. Move it to a WordPress Guidelines skill so the site agent and other clients can discover it, but do not overwrite edits after setup.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Run wordpress-router and wp-project-triage to classify the repo and locate the plugin entrypoint
Step 2: Route to wp-knowledge because the task mentions WordPress Guidelines, Knowledge storage, agent-discoverable skill storage, and compatibility with legacy wp_guideline behavior

Step 3: Confirm whether the target runtime exposes the complete wp_knowledge/wp_knowledge_type and /wp/v2/knowledge backend, the legacy wp_guideline/wp_guideline_type and /wp/v2/guidelines backend, or the wpcom/guidelines ability
Step 4: Prefer wp_knowledge for new writes when it is available, and use legacy wp_guideline only as a compatibility fallback or read surface
Step 5: Choose the skill type rather than guideline, memory, note/artifact, plan, or instruction, registering or verifying the type if the runtime does not provide it
Step 6: Resolve or create the active backend's type term by slug and assign by term id
Step 7: Create or update a post with stable slug, title, excerpt, content, status, author, and the matching type taxonomy
Step 8: Preserve user edits after setup by using an idempotent seeding strategy such as a plugin-specific seed hash or a code-defined default guideline
Step 9: Keep site-wide publish behavior behind an administrator-controlled setup path or explicit user intent
Step 10: Verify REST or ability discovery and permission behavior for private/published rows
success_criteria: Uses wp_knowledge/wp_knowledge_type for new writes when Knowledge is available
Does not mix wp_knowledge with wp_guideline_type or wp_guideline with wp_knowledge_type
Mentions legacy wp_guideline compatibility only as fallback or read compatibility
Stores the short discovery text in excerpt and full procedure in content
Does not clobber user-edited content on later runs
Respects WordPress capabilities and authenticated REST or wpcom/guidelines behavior
Mentions graceful degradation when neither Knowledge nor legacy Guidelines are available
